column9: Linear floor: balanced recall across classes but heavy Pass/Distinction confusion; accuracy sacrificed for even class treatment.
Non-linearity lifts accuracy and AUC over Exp 1, but the forest hides in the majority class: Distinction recall collapses despite balanced weights.
Capacity control recovers part of the minority recall Exp 2 lost while keeping its accuracy advantage; CV-chosen depth/leaf settings shrink the variance gap.
Negative result: Distinction recall (~0.25) beats the raw forest but stays far below the tuned forest's ~0.49 — resampling lost to reweighting here. Precision rose instead, and AUC slipped slightly.
Matches the classical models' ranking quality without beating it; class weights restore even per-class recall similar to Exp 1 but at higher accuracy.
Regularisation closes Exp 5's val-loss divergence and lets training run ~30 epochs instead of 19; best NN AUC and Distinction recall so far, paid for with a couple of points of raw accuracy.
Structured inputs match Exp 6 with about a third of the parameters; the architecture encodes the heatmap's behaviour/demographics independence rather than spending capacity learning it.
Dropping the Fail/Withdrawn distinction yields the best single AUC of the notebook; threshold choice becomes an interpretable teacher-facing dial.
